item.title: 환절기 찾아오는 붉은 발진과 각질…'건선' 주의보
item.summary:
아침저녁으로 쌀쌀한 바람이 불고 공기가 건조해지는 가을과 겨울철에는 만성 피부질환인 '건선'이 악화하기 쉬우므로 각별한 주의가 필요하다. 건선은 피부에 붉은 발진과 함께 하얀 각질이 반복해서 발생하는 고질적인 질환으로, 국내에서도 많은 환자가 겪고 있다.
건강보험심사평가원의 통계 자료에 따르면, 건선으로 진료를 받은 환자는 2021년부터 지난해까지 매해 15만명을 웃돌았으며, 2025년에는 15만4987명에 달한 것으로 집계됐다. 건선은 단순히 외견상 드러나는 피부 문제를 넘어 관절을 비롯한 전신 건강에 영향을 미칠 수 있다. 강동경희대병원 피부과 권순효 교수와 함께 건선의 발생 원인과 치료법, 예방 관리법에 대해 알아봤다.
면역세포 이상과 환경적 요인 복합 작용…타인에게 옮지 않아
건선은 우리 몸의 면역체계에 이상이 생겨 피부 세포가 정상보다 과도하게 빠르게 증식하면서 발생하는 질환이다. 이 과정에서 피부 위에 비듬 같은 하얀 각질이 겹겹이 쌓이게 된다. 구체적으로는 면역세포 중 하나인 T세포가 비정상적으로 활성화되면서 분비되는 물질들이 피부를 자극해 만성적인 염증을 유발하는 것이 주된 기전이다.
여기에 유전적인 요인과 더불어 건조한 기후, 물리적인 피부 자극, 과도한 스트레스 등 다양한 환경적 요인이 결합해 증상을 발현시키거나 악화시킨다. 유전적 성향이 강해 가족력이 있는 경우 더욱 세심한 주의가 요구된다. 다만 병변 부위에 나타나는 각질 때문에 전염병으로 오인받는 경우가 많지만, 타인에게 절대 옮지 않는 비전염성 질환이다.
초기에는 좁쌀 모양 발진…봄철인 4~5월에 환자 수 정점 달해
질환 초기에는 좁쌀 크기의 작은 발진으로 시작되지만, 시간이 지나면서 그 위로 붉고 두꺼운 각질이 광범위하게 덮이게 된다. 주로 마찰이나 외부 자극을 자주 받는 무릎, 팔꿈치, 엉덩이, 두피 등에 흔히 발생하며 증세가 심해지면 병변들이 서로 뭉쳐 전신으로 번지기도 한다. 통상적으로 발진의 형태와 발생 부위를 육안으로 확인해 진단하지만, 일반적인 피부 건조증과 구별하고 정확한 진행 상태를 진단하기 위해 국소 마취 후 피부 조직의 일부를 떼어내 검사하는 조직 검사를 병행하기도 한다.
건선은 대기가 선선해지는 가을부터 발현하기 시작해 겨울을 지나며 점차 악화되는 경향을 보인다. 2025년 심평원 자료를 살펴보면, 가을과 겨울철 내내 건조한 환경에 노출돼 누적된 증상 때문에 이듬해 봄철인 4~5월에 환자 수가 4만명을 넘어서며 정점을 찍는 것으로 확인됐다.
권순효 교수는 "찬바람이 부는 시기에는 보습 관리에 철저를 기해야 하며 고름을 동반한 물집 등 급성 악화 현상이 나타나지 않도록 주의해야 한다"고 설명했다. 아울러 "계절 변화에 따라 증상이 일시적으로 좋아진 것처럼 보여도 임의로 치료를 중단하지 말고 일 년 내내 꾸준히 치료에 임해야 한다"고 덧붙였다.
관절염에서 대사증후군까지…전신 합병증 동반 위험
건선을 제때 치료하지 않고 방치할 경우 염증 반응이 피부에만 머무르지 않고 혈관을 통해 전신으로 퍼져 다양한 합병증을 유발할 수 있다. 기상 시 손가락이나 발가락 관절이 뻣뻣해지고 부어올라 물건을 쥐는 힘이 약해지는 '건선 관절염'이 대표적인 사례다.
또한 증상이 무거울수록 당뇨병이나 고혈압 같은 대사증후군은 물론이고 심근경색, 뇌졸중 등 생명을 위협하는 심혈관계 질환의 발병 확률이 눈에 띄게 높아진다. 따라서 단순한 피부 치료를 넘어 전신 건강을 보존하기 위해서라도 조기 진단과 적극적인 대처가 필수적이다.
증상에 따른 3단계 치료법 적용…일상 속 보습 습관 병행돼야 효과적
건선의 치료는 증상의 경중에 따라 크게 세 가지 단계로 나뉘어 진행된다. 대증적인 초기 단계에는 피부 염증을 완화하는 비타민 D 유도체 및 스테로이드 성분의 연고를 환부에 바르는 국소 치료를 시행한다. 만약 발진 부위가 넓어지면 면역 반응 자체를 조절하는 경구 약제를 복용하거나, 피부 재생을 유도하는 광선치료를 함께 적용한다.
이러한 기존 치료법으로도 호전되지 않는 중증 환자에게는 건선의 원인이 되는 특정 면역 물질만 선택적으로 억제하는 '생물학적 제제' 주사 치료를 통해 증상을 크게 호전시킬 수 있다. 근래에는 부작용을 줄이고 예후를 좋게 만들기 위해 여러 치료 수단을 적절히 조합하는 복합 치료도 활발히 이뤄지고 있다.
체계적인 병원 치료와 더불어 일상생활 속에서 올바른 습관을 유지해야 재발을 효과적으로 억제할 수 있다. 가장 핵심적인 수칙은 피부 수분을 적절히 유지하고 자극을 주지 않는 것이다. 뜨거운 물로 장시간 목욕을 하거나 사우나에 자주 가는 행동은 피해야 하며, 미지근한 물로 가볍게 샤워를 마치는 것이 좋다.
특히 피부에 물리적 상처를 입히는 때 밀기는 절대로 금물이다. 샤워 직후에는 보습제를 충분히 도포해 피부 장벽을 보호해야 하며, 전신 염증을 심화시키는 음주와 흡연은 반드시 멀리해야 한다.
권순효 교수는 "최근 치료제의 발달로 환자 상태에 따른 맞춤형 처방이 가능해진 만큼 치료를 쉽게 포기해서는 안 된다"고 강조하며 "전문의와 함께 체계적인 계획을 수립하고 올바른 생활 습관을 지켜나간다면 충분히 정상적인 일상을 누릴 수 있다"고 조언했다.

item.title: 산업약사회, 내달 11일 '헬스케어 산업약사 커넥트' 개최
item.summary:
의료기기·건강기능식품·화장품 등 헬스케어 산업의 정책·규제 변화를 살펴보고, 제약을 넘어 약사의 전문성을 발휘할 기회를 모색하는 자리가 마련된다.
한국산업약사회는 오는 11월 11일 서울 양재동 aT센터에서 '2026 헬스케어 산업약사 커넥트'를 개최한다.
이번 행사는 산업 간 경계가 흐려지는 가운데 의료기기·건강기능식품·화장품 등 각 산업의 구조와 정책·규제 변화를 이해하고, 약사의 전문성을 활용할 기회를 찾기 위해 마련됐다.
다양한 분야에서 활동하는 산업약사들이 현장 경험을 나누고 협력의 접점을 모색하는 자리이기도 하다.
행사는 1부 주제 강연과 2부 네트워킹으로 구성된다. 1부에서는 '정책 변화와 산업약사의 기회'를 주제로 세 가지 강연이 진행된다.
천경석 헬스케어위원장(HTL Biotechnology)은 '제약을 넘어 확장되는 바이오헬스 산업'을 주제로 시장 변화와 새로운 기회를 살펴본다.
이어 이영주 전문위원(법무법인 화우)이 '의료기기·건강기능식품 : 규제 대응 사례에서 사업 기회를 읽다'를 통해 규제 대응 전략과 사례를 소개한다.
윤미옥 한국보건산업진흥원 PD는 '화장품: K-뷰티의 성장과 규제 변화, 산업약사의 역할을 넓히다'를 주제로 산업 변화와 약사의 역할을 조명한다.
2부에서는 참석자들이 분야별 실무 경험과 관심사를 공유하며 자유롭게 교류하는 네트워킹 시간을 갖는다.
한국산업약사회는 이번 행사를 계기로 제약을 넘어 다양한 헬스케어 분야에서 산업약사의 역할을 구체화하고, 분야 간 협력과 지속적인 교류를 강화할 방침이다.
참가 대상은 의료기기·건강기능식품·화장품·원료의약품(API)·디지털헬스 등 헬스케어 산업에 재직 중이거나 해당 분야에 관심이 있는 약사다. 선착순 50명을 모집하며, 참가비는 2만원으로 한국산업약사회 회원은 무료다.

item.title: 인천성모병원 김영주 간호사, 복지부장관 표창…호스피스 공로
item.summary:
가톨릭대학교 인천성모병원은 호스피스완화의료센터 김영주 가정형 호스피스 전담간호사가 호스피스·완화의료 발전에 기여한 공로로 보건복지부장관 표창을 받았다고 26일 밝혔다.
김 간호사는 최근 서울 용산구 나인트리 프리미어 로카우스 호텔에서 열린 '제14회 호스피스의 날' 기념식에서 표창을 받았다.
이번 표창은 호스피스·완화의료 현장에서 환자와 가족의 삶의 질 향상에 기여하고, 관련 분야의 발전과 인식 확산에 힘쓴 유공자에게 수여됐다.
김 간호사는 가정형 호스피스 전담간호사로서 말기환자가 익숙한 가정에서 가족과 함께 삶의 마지막 시간을 보낼 수 있도록 방문간호를 제공해 왔다.
환자의 통증과 신체적 증상을 관리하는 동시에 환자와 가족의 심리·사회적 어려움까지 살피는 등 전인적 돌봄을 실천해 왔다.
또한 국내외 학술대회와 교육활동을 통해 가정형 호스피스 현장에서 쌓은 경험과 전문지식을 공유하고, 호스피스·완화의료 종사자의 전문성과 실무 역량 강화에도 기여했다.
김영주 간호사는 "이번 수상은 환자와 가족의 곁을 함께 지켜 온 호스피스팀 모두의 노력 덕분이라고 생각한다"며 "앞으로도 환자와 가족이 익숙한 공간에서 삶의 마지막 순간까지 존엄함을 지킬 수 있도록 따뜻한 돌봄을 실천하겠다"고 말했다.

item.title: An ensemble clustering typology of long-term care policies: evidence from 30 OECD countries
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Population ageing is pushing long-term care (LTC) to the centre of welfare-state reform debates, yet countries differ markedly in how they finance, regulate, and supply LTC. Existing typologies are largely qualitative, suffer from limited reproducibility and inconsistent country coverage, and constrain cross-national policy learning. OBJECTIVE: To construct an empirically grounded, reproducible typology of LTC systems across 30 OECD countries and to evaluate its stability and limits through systematic validation. METHODS: We use a clustering ensemble combining fuzzy c-means (FCM), self-organising maps (SOM), and partitioning around medoids (PAM). The classification draws on ten indicators spanning four dimensions: supply, demand, financing, and access, regulation and outcomes. We validate the typology through internal cluster indices, descriptive cluster profiling, and sensitivity analyses, including random subsampling. RESULTS: We identify seven LTC system types. Three broadly recover established welfare-state groupings: a high-supply, publicly financed Nordic type; a low-supply, family-reliance Eastern European type; and a Southern European familialism type. Four reveal finer distinctions or substantive departures from institutional classifications: Sweden and the United States cluster together along outcome-based dimensions, the United Kingdom aligns with continental Europe rather than the Anglo-Saxon liberal regime, and two further types capture mixed or transitional systems. The seven-cluster solution is stable across algorithmic parameters and random subsampling. CONCLUSIONS: The typology offers a transparent and reproducible benchmark for cross-country comparison and a tool for evidence-based policy learning. By identifying countries that converge on outcomes despite divergent institutional characteristics, it highlights peer comparators relevant to LTC reform under demographic and fiscal pressure.

item.title: Well-being and healthcare work over the pandemic
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Well-being in the healthcare sector is of substantial policy relevance, given persistent labour shortages and the central role of subjective well-being in worker productivity and retention. OBJECTIVE: We investigate changes in healthcare workers' life satisfaction since the onset of the pandemic relative to workers in other essential and non-essential sectors, and examine the role of pandemic severity and subsequent policy responses in explaining these differences. METHODS: We use thirteen waves of quarterly panel data from the COME-HERE dataset, which collects information on respondents in five European countries from April 2020 to August 2024, and estimate linear regressions via OLS. RESULTS: The life satisfaction of healthcare workers is always higher than that of other essential workers and non-essential workers. During the pandemic, the pandemic death rate had a negative effect on life satisfaction that was three times larger for healthcare workers. At the same time, lockdown stringency reduced the life satisfaction of workers in every sector other than healthcare. CONCLUSIONS: As pandemic death rates and lockdown stringency mostly moved hand-in-hand, the higher life satisfaction of healthcare workers persisted throughout and after the pandemic possibly reflecting the meaningful nature of their jobs. At the same time, the negative impact of pandemic severity on workers' well-being is especially pronounced among healthcare workers, highlighting the importance of supporting their well-being during public health crises to sustain healthcare system performance.

item.title: Operationalising value-based payment: a decision-support framework for health system reform
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Health systems worldwide face mounting pressure to deliver better outcomes with constrained resources. Improving productivity therefore depends not only on operational efficiency but also on payment approaches that align incentives with value. Value-Based Payment (VBP) models seek to reward quality and efficiency rather than service volume, yet their design and sequencing remain complex, particularly in publicly oriented health systems where sustainability and equity are core objectives. OBJECTIVE: To develop and validate a decision-support framework that assists policymakers and managers in designing and implementing VBP models to improve system productivity and sustainability. METHODS: A two-stage conceptual study was conducted. First, a scoping review of 14 conceptual articles (2015-2025) was undertaken following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Second, a targeted expert survey (n = 10; response rate = 21.7%) validated and refined the framework's structure. Experts from multiple countries assessed the relevance, coherence, and completeness of framework domains using structured quantitative and qualitative feedback. RESULTS: The validated framework comprises six iterative phases: (1) Stakeholder Insight and Context Analysis, (2) Problem Definition and Value Proposition, (3) Strategic Co-Design, (4) Operational Design, (5) Pilot Assessment, and (6) Full-Scale Deployment. These stages are supported by cross-cutting components linking value definition, incentive alignment, and organisational readiness. Expert consensus was strongest for early analytical phases and leadership-related capabilities (median confidence >80%), indicating strong conceptual alignment and practical applicability across contexts. CONCLUSIONS: The framework offers a structured roadmap for designing VBP reforms that enhance productivity and financial sustainability without compromising care quality or equity. It supports policymakers in sequencing reforms, aligning incentives, and ensuring readiness for value-based transformation, directly contributing to policy debates on improving health system productivity.

analysis.title_ko: 가치기반 지불의 실행: 보건의료체계 개혁을 위한 의사결정 지원 프레임워크
analysis.summary_ko: 공공 중심 체계에서 가치기반 지불(VBP) 모형의 설계와 도입 순서를 안내하는 프레임워크를 제시했다(Health Policy). 성과 기반 보상 확대를 논의하는 한국에 참고가 된다.

item.title: How do countries design and govern staffing levels? A comparative analysis of European approaches
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Staffing levels are increasingly used to help address workforce shortages, safeguard quality and support health system performance. However, comparative evidence on why countries define staffing levels and how these policies are designed and governed remains limited. OBJECTIVE: By comparing approaches across countries, the study provides new evidence on the governance and implementation of staffing levels and supports policy learning on designing staffing policies that are both responsive to changing population and workforce needs and aligned with broader health system goals. METHODS: This article draws on a report developed with the European Commission's Expert Group on Health Systems Performance Assessment which conducted a comparative analysis of staffing-level policies across European Union Member States and Norway, using a structured questionnaire, complemented by a policy workshop and Policy Focus Group. RESULTS: Countries employ fixed, flexible and hybrid staffing approaches across health system sectors in pursuit of different policy objectives. These choices reflect differences in service organisation, workforce capacity and governance arrangements. Staffing policies are governed through varying combinations of national regulation, decentralised decision-making, professional standards and provider-level implementation, and are unevenly integrated with workforce planning, financing and education. CONCLUSIONS: There is no universally applicable staffing model. Effective staffing policy requires context-sensitive design, clear governance and stronger integration with wider health workforce and health system policies. Comparative monitoring can support policy learning without imposing uniform staffing benchmarks across Europe.

item.title: Health systems' responses to climate change: an umbrella review of systematic reviews
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Climate change places increasing pressure on health systems. They must both reduce their negative impact on the environment and strengthen resilience to climate-related risks. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize and map the evidence from systematic reviews on the scope and effectiveness of climate change mitigation and adaptation actions in health systems. METHODS: An umbrella review of systematic reviews examining health system responses to climate change was conducted. The review followed the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological guidelines and adhered to the PRISMA checklist. The included systematic reviews had to meet two overarching criteria: at least two databases were searched, and a predefined instrument was used to assess the quality or risk of bias of the included studies. RESULTS: Forty-six systematic reviews published between 2020 and 2026 were included, covering 1,175 individual studies. Most reviews (41/46) focused exclusively on mitigation strategies, with evidence concentrated around major greenhouse gas emission hotspots: surgical procedures; radiology; pharmaceuticals; solid waste; and transportation of patients and staff. Across these areas, some mitigation strategies were associated with environmental and economic co-benefits, although the underlying evidence was heterogeneous and often of low to moderate quality. In contrast, only a small number of reviews addressed climate adaptation and health system resilience. CONCLUSIONS: Existing evidence provides practical guidance on effective climate mitigation actions. The limited number of systematic reviews on climate adaptation highlights a gap in the evidence base. Translating mitigation evidence into clinical guidelines and policies and strengthening research on adaptation could support more systematic climate action in health systems.

item.title: From technologies to capabilities: Sustaining system-level digital transformation in Singapore public healthcare - a NASSS-informed policy analysis
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Digital transformation has become a central policy concern for health systems seeking to address rising demand, workforce constraints, and increasing care complexity. While digital technologies, automation, and artificial intelligence (AI) offer significant promise, many initiatives struggle to move beyond pilots to achieve sustained, system-wide impact. OBJECTIVE: This paper applies the Non-adoption, Abandonment, Scale-up, Spread, and Sustainability (NASSS) framework to guide system-level analysis of the digital transformation journey of a large public healthcare system in Singapore. We retrospectively analyse three interrelated programmes: a digital technology driven care transformation programme, a citizen developer-driven workflow automation, and an enterprise level AI deployment platform. METHODOLOGY: Using a qualitative, retrospective case study approach, we examine how these programmes map across the seven NASSS domains and how interactions between domains shaped adoption, scale-up, and sustainability. RESULTS: The analysis highlights the importance of organisational capability, governance, and workforce development as primary enablers of sustained digital transformation, often outweighing the characteristics of individual technologies. Defining the intervention at a system level enabled horizontal integration and scalability but also introduced challenges in articulating patient-level value and evaluating impact. CONCLUSION: Applying NASSS beyond disease, or technology-specific, interventions reveals both its strengths and limitations. While the framework provides a useful structure for understanding complexity, it requires adaptation when applied to institutional or system-level programmes. The findings reaffirm that policymakers and system leaders should focus not only on adopting digital tools, but on building the organisational and human capabilities needed to responsibly scale, embed, and sustain digital innovation over time.

analysis.title_ko: 기술에서 역량으로: 싱가포르 공공의료 디지털 전환의 지속 조건 — NASSS 정책 분석
analysis.summary_ko: 시범사업을 넘어 체계 전반의 디지털 전환을 지속시키는 조건을 싱가포르 사례로 분석했다.

item.title: The health and care workforce in Europe's emerging health security architecture: A comparative assessment of seven EU countries
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Growing hybrid and military threats are converging with health and care workforce poly-crises, placing increasing pressure on health system resilience. OBJECTIVES: This study examines how European Union (EU) member states protect and prepare the workforce for health security threats and how these measures impact resilience. METHODS: A qualitative comparative assessment of EU health security policy and seven country cases was performed, including Czechia, Finland, Germany, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal and Romania. A structured topic guide informed data collection in April 2026, drawing on expert input and secondary sources. RESULTS: Since COVID-19, health security institutions and defence-related preparedness have expanded substantially across countries. Three broad patterns emerge within a new health security and resilience architecture shaped by health systems, defence strategies and workforce conditions, but also important common trends: workforce stability and resilience remain marginal within these emerging architectures and critical gaps in protection and preparedness, and priority of military-centred approaches threaten health system resilience. DISCUSSION: Investment in military-centred defence remains inefficient if not aligned with workforce resilience, including preparedness, physical and mental health protection, equity and gender equality. Key challenges for policymakers are to shift from military- and infrastructure-focused preparedness toward integrated strategies with the workforce as foundational pillar of critical security infrastructure and an operational indicator of resilience, and to build capacity for the implementation of new security policies. CONCLUSIONS: The EU needs a coordinated workforce-centred strategy with a sustainable budget that strengthens preparedness, protection, governance capacity, research and implementation to improve resilience under crisis and defence conditions.

item.title: Should the geriatrician host the party? Person-centred hospital care in ageing societies requires placing geriatrics at the centre of care
item.summary: As populations age, multimorbidity and frailty increasingly characterize hospital admissions, exposing the limits of traditional disease-specific and organ-centred models of care. Older adults with complex care needs face higher risks of hospitalization, readmission, functional decline, and fragmented care pathways, while hospitals remain insufficiently aligned with these realities. Despite strong evidence for the clinical and economic benefits of Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment (CGA) and geriatric-led care, geriatrics often remains peripheral to everyday clinical practice and hospital governance. Integrated geriatric models have consistently demonstrated improved outcomes, including fewer complications, reduced institutionalization, shorter lengths of stay, and greater cost-effectiveness. Person-centred hospital care in ageing societies requires placing geriatrics at the centre of care. This includes structurally embedding geriatric principles across clinical pathways, leadership and governance structures, workforce development, and digital systems. Recognizing geriatrics as a supraspecialty is essential for delivering coordinated, sustainable, and future-ready hospital care for older adults living with frailty and multimorbidity.

item.title: Designing a National Suicide Prevention Strategy (2026-2031): Insights from Malta's Whole-of-Government and Whole-of-Society Model
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Suicide remains a global public health concern, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to advocate for comprehensive national prevention strategies. Despite a historically low suicide mortality rate, Malta has experienced rising mental health challenges linked to rapid socioeconomic transformation. This paper analyses the development of Malta's inaugural National Suicide Prevention Strategy (NSPS) 2026-2031, which utilises an integrated whole-of-government and whole-of-society model. REFORM CONTENT: The strategy is built upon a six-pillar implementation framework: (1) Coordination and Organisation, (2) Support and Treatment, (3) Restriction of Access to Means, (4) Awareness and Knowledge, (5) Prevention and Health Promotion and (6) Quality Assurance and Expertise. Key actions include establishing an Acute Psychiatric Centre, enhancing 24/7 crisis services, and implementing specialised gatekeeper training. The strategy was informed by consultations with over 40 stakeholders from diverse public, private, and community sectors, a literature review, WHO guidance, and European best practices. EXPECTED RESULTS: The NSPS aims to further reduce Malta's suicide mortality rate by optimising service accessibility and population-level mental health literacy. Key outcomes focus on the earlier identification of at-risk individuals through standardised gatekeeper training, timely clinical interventions, seamless care transitions, and enhanced data collection. CONCLUSIONS: This strategy prioritises intersectoral collaboration and measurable targets to enhance prevention efforts. Malta's experience demonstrates how high-growth nations can utilise multisectoral governance to mitigate the mental health impacts of rapid urbanisation and demographic shifts. Long-term efficacy remains contingent upon sustained investment, rigorous evaluation, and adaptive implementation to ensure the strategy's resilience within evolving demographic contexts.

item.title: Characteristics of medical malpractice claims over 22 years: a population-based analysis in Catalonia, Spain
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Data on malpractice claims provide crucial healthcare-related information to stakeholders: policymakers, insurance companies, patients, and the society in general. Population-based studies on professional liability claims are scarce. OBJECTIVE: To assess the characteristics of medical malpractice claims over 22 years in Catalonia, Spain, covering a descriptive period (2000-2022) and a population-based trend analysis period (2000-2018). METHODS: Retrospective longitudinal analysis of malpractice claims records obtained from insurance policies established through the jointly coordinated risk-coverage agreement between the Council of Medical Associations of Catalonia (CCMC) and the public health administration, via the Catalan Health Service (CatSalut). Changes in population-based malpractice claims overall and regarding hospitalisation, surgery, obstetrics, and emergency care were assessed. Claim rates by activity type were calculated and trends assessed using linear regression and the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for time-delay distribution. RESULTS: While Catalonia's population showed a 22.3% increase (2000-2018), total medical malpractice claims decreased by 9.5% and population-adjusted claim rates (2000-2018) dropped by 26.1% (P < 0.0005). Surgical claim rates fell by 34.0%, obstetric claims by 3.7%, and emergency-related claims by 20.5%. Hospitalization-related rates remained stable. The mean delay between the incident and claim filing was 23.9 months. CONCLUSIONS: In contrast to the general perception, medical malpractice claims in Catalonia have declined or stabilized over the past two decades especially when adjusted for healthcare activity. The Catalan insurance model enables robust population-level data, providing a unique tool for medicolegal risk monitoring. These findings support the use of standardized population-based parameters and argue for international comparison of health management models to inform policy and enhance patient safety.

item.title: Decomposing health-service volume growth in Türkiye: volume-based physician productivity and physician-density growth in a 12-country OECD comparison
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Türkiye's 2003 Health Transformation Programme, combining insurance expansion, primary-care reform and activity-based supplementary payment, was followed by one of the fastest expansions of health-service use among OECD countries with comparable data. Whether it was met by adding physicians or by higher recorded volume per physician has not been quantified. OBJECTIVE: To decompose Türkiye's health-service volume growth (1990-2019) into physician-density and volume-per-physician margins, and compare the pathway with OECD countries meeting the coverage criteria. METHODS: Descriptive analysis of OECD Health Statistics and IHME Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 series, 1990-2019. A log-additive identity decomposes per-person volume growth into recorded service volume per physician and physician density. Cross-country comparisons use period means (1990-2002 versus 2003-2019) in a 12-country core selected by an ex ante coverage rule, with sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: Consultations per physician rose from 1444 (1990) to 5026 (2019). Volume per physician accounted for 82% of consultation growth in 2003-2008 (69% over 2003-2019), growing 11.2 log points a year against 3.6 pre-reform as density growth slowed. The increase was the largest of 12 countries with comparable coverage; comparator medians were negative. Medical-graduate output stayed below its pre-reform mean until 2015. CONCLUSIONS: The timing is consistent with demand-side reform preceding growth in the training pipeline, most volume growth occurring through higher recorded volume per physician. Reforms expected to raise service use should include prospective workforce planning and monitoring of volume relative to capacity.

item.title: Mandatory reporting of healthcare-associated infections: a global comparative policy analysis using Kingdon's multiple streams framework
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) impose a substantial burden on healthcare systems worldwide. Despite strong evidence of their impact and preventability, national infection prevention and control (IPC) surveillance systems remain inconsistently implemented. In contrast, the COVID-19 pandemic catalyzed rapid surveillance reforms, highlighting policy conditions that facilitate surveillance-based IPC strategies. OBJECTIVE: To examine policy factors influencing the implementation of national HAI surveillance and compare the policy window created during COVID-19 with the more limited political attention devoted to HAI surveillance. METHODS: A qualitative comparative policy analysis was conducted using Kingdon's Multiple Streams Framework. World Health Organization policy documents, peer-reviewed literature, reports from international public health organizations, and selected national policy documents were synthesized to examine how the problem, policy, and political streams influenced the implementation of HAI surveillance. RESULTS: The problem stream was well established, with extensive evidence of the burden of HAIs. The policy stream was similarly well developed through established surveillance frameworks, whose feasibility was demonstrated during the COVID-19 pandemic. In contrast, the political stream remained comparatively weak, characterized by fragmented political commitment, inconsistent legal mandates, limited public visibility, and variable implementation across countries. Consequently, convergence of the three streams required to sustain a policy window for HAI surveillance remained incomplete. CONCLUSION: The principal barrier to national HAI surveillance is insufficient alignment of the problem, policy, and political streams rather than a lack of evidence or technical solutions. Strengthening political commitment through legal mandates, sustained investment, governance, and advocacy is essential to institutionalize surveillance systems and strengthen long-term IPC.

item.title: What health reforms promise and what evaluations measure: A comparative policy analysis of reform evaluation in six predominantly tax-funded high-income countries
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Predominantly tax-funded high-income countries are undertaking large-scale reforms to address demographic, workforce and fiscal pressures, digital transformation and fragmented care. Reforms in Australia, England, Canada, Denmark, Norway and Sweden emphasise integration, primary and community care, and sustainability, but their evaluation alignment remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: To compare alignment between national reform objectives and evaluation models across six predominantly tax-funded high-income systems, identifying where reform promises translate into measurable progress. METHODS: We conducted a mixed-methods document review and comparative policy analysis. Initial extraction occurred during April-June 2025, with targeted updating and source verification in May 2026. Government, agency, independent organisation and policy documents in English, Danish, Swedish and Norwegian were included. Structured extraction and explicit coding rules mapped reform objectives and evaluation indicators to an adapted World Health Organization Health System Performance Assessment framework across Functions, Intermediate Objectives and Final Goals. RESULTS: Reforms covered system Functions and most Intermediate Objectives. Evaluation indicators were strongest where routine administrative data were available, particularly activity, financing, access, utilisation, service efficiency and selected safety measures. Measurement was weaker for people-centredness, integration, continuity, prevention, health improvement, financial protection and system equity. The recurring problem was misalignment between reform ambitions and what evaluation models measured. CONCLUSIONS: These six systems showed a recurrent gap between reform ambition and evaluation practice. Evaluation could be strengthened by planning at inception, pairing objectives with indicators, improving cross-sector data infrastructure, transparently reporting evaluation resourcing, and strengthening governance for longitudinal learning and accountability. These findings inform evaluation design in comparable tax-funded systems.

item.title: Health Data Utilities as Essential Public Infrastructure: A Cooperative Federalism Architecture
item.summary: UNLABELLED: Policy Points Federal interoperability networks transport standardized clinical data but do not aggregate, enrich, or analyze the state-governed data that clinical practice, public health, and Medicaid administration require locally. State-designated health data utilities fill this structural gap through a cooperative federalism architecture in which states build and operate local data infrastructure and the federal government provides regulatory flexibility and financial incentives. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act requires states to implement twice-yearly redeterminations beginning in 2027, creating a unified enforcement cycle that no existing infrastructure can absorb at scale. The health data utility offers the most administratively viable architecture for preventing catastrophic procedural disenrollments as state budgets contract. A four-layer financing model distributes financial risk across state general funds, Medicaid enhanced matching, payer enrichment revenue, and value-based payment integration. Federal action should formalize a health data utility profile within the Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement and confirm enhanced Medicaid matching for shared infrastructure. CONTEXT: Federal interoperability initiatives like Trusted Exchange Framework and Common Agreement transport clinical records across boundaries but fail to aggregate and enrich state-governed datasets, including Medicaid claims, prescription monitoring records, and social service registries. This fragmentation creates fiscal and administrative liability for states, exacerbated by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act's mandate for twice-yearly Medicaid redeterminations and work verifications beginning in 2027 amidst tightening state budgets. METHODS: Synthesizing health information exchange literature, existing state operational models (Maryland, Indiana, California, North Carolina), and federal statutory requirements, we propose a cooperative federalism governance model, technical data architecture, and multi-payer financing strategy for state-designated health data utilities (HDUs). FINDINGS: We propose an HDU architecture that can be adapted across multiple states, designed to directly advance clinical care delivery by functioning as an enrichment layer integrated natively into electronic health record workflows. By synthesizing longitudinal clinical encounters, controlled substance histories, claims, and social needs registries in real time, the proposed utility would deliver actionable predictive risk scores and automated point-of-care alerts to prevent avoidable readmissions, curtail redundant advanced imaging, and coordinate cross-sector interventions for high-risk patients. Operationally, the model pairs this bedside enrichment with automated eligibility and frailty verification, ensuring high-need individuals maintain continuous access to essential clinical services. CONCLUSIONS: Clinical data fragmentation is rooted in governance silos rather than technical barriers. Establishing state-designated HDUs through a cooperative federalism model bridges bedside clinical practice, public health, and Medicaid administration. HDUs provide the integrated infrastructure necessary to prevent clinical crises, protect vulnerable populations, and improve care delivery at scale across the United States.

item.title: State and Local Syringe Distribution Laws and the Presence of Syringe Services Programs
item.summary: IMPORTANCE: Syringe services programs (SSPs) are an evidence-based intervention to reduce bloodborne disease transmission and other risks related to injection drug use; however, SSP access is uneven. State and local syringe distribution laws may influence variation in the presence and number of SSPs across local jurisdictions. OBJECTIVE: To assess the association between state and local syringe distribution laws and presence of publicly listed SSPs in a sample of US cities. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cross-sectional study linked state and local laws with information on publicly reported SSPs in 2024 for the largest US municipalities and census-designated places (localities). The outcomes of policy exposure in SSP presence and total number of SSP locations among localities with at least 1 SSP were estimated using a 2-part negative binomial hurdle model, adjusting for state and local policy and demographic and health characteristics. The study team collected the legal data from January 11, 2023, through May 7, 2024. EXPOSURE: State and local syringe distribution policy environment as of December 31, 2022, categorized from most restrictive (state prohibition) to least restrictive (neither state nor locality prohibits syringe distribution). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Publicly reported SSP presence (binary) and total count of SSP locations within each locality as of February 2024. RESULTS: In this study using data from 482 US localities, there was at least 1 SSP in 181 (37.6%) localities. Localities with the least restrictive legal environment had increased odds of SSP presence (adjusted odds ratio, 16.3; 95% CI, 6.0-44.1) compared with those with the most restrictive legal environment. Among localities with 1 or more SSP, localities in the least restrictive legal environment or a legal environment that exempted SSPs from a syringe distribution prohibition had increased rates of SSPs, relative to the most restrictive legal environment (rate ratio for least restrictive policy environment, 2.7; 95% CI, 1.1-6.4; rate ratio for legal environment that exempts SSPs from prohibition, 2.4; 95% CI, 1.1-5.6). Overall, policies that exempted SSPs from syringe distribution prohibitions and those with no syringe distribution prohibitions had the highest estimated SSP counts (1.9 SSPs; 95% CI, 1.5-2.4; 1.5 SSPs; 95% CI, 1.1-1.9, respectively). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that state and local syringe distribution laws were associated with publicly listed SSP presence. Legal environments that prohibit or restrict syringe distribution may limit the presence and total number of SSPs, highlighting the role of policy context in shaping access to harm-reduction services.

item.title: Local Wealth Inequality and Working-Age Mortality in US Counties
item.summary: IMPORTANCE: Household wealth is associated with health and survival, but little is known about whether wealth inequality is associated with mortality as a contextual exposure. OBJECTIVE: To examine the association between local wealth inequality and age-adjusted all-cause mortality across US counties over 5 decades. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This longitudinal, county-level study of up to 18 344 county-year observations from 1970 to 2019 linked restricted-access, all-cause mortality data from the US National Center for Health Statistics with county-level population and sociodemographic information and commuting zone estimates of household wealth inequality from the GEOWEALTH-US database. US counties were observed at decennial intervals from 1970 to 2019, with 2019 mortality used for the final period to avoid distortion from the COVID-19 pandemic. After listwise deletion, the estimation sample included up to 18 344 county-year observations nested in 732 commuting zones. EXPOSURE: Commuting zone Gini index score of household net wealth inequality. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: County-specific, sex-specific, age-adjusted all-cause mortality rates for ages 25 to 44, 45 to 54, and 55 to 64 years, modeled on the natural log scale. RESULTS: In adjusted 2-way fixed-effects models with county, year, and state by year fixed effects, higher local wealth inequality was associated with higher mortality across all sex-age groups. Unstandardized regression coefficients (b) were 1.72 (95% CI, 0.99-2.45), 1.57 (95% CI, 0.96-2.18), and 1.11 (95% CI, 0.65-1.57) for female individuals aged 25 to 44, 45 to 54, and 55 to 64 years, respectively, and 0.75 (95% CI, 0.12-1.37), 0.71 (95% CI, 0.27-1.14), and 0.66 (95% CI, 0.24-1.08), respectively, for male individuals in the same age groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this aggregate longitudinal cross-sectional study, increases in local wealth inequality were associated with within-county increases in working-age mortality. These findings suggest that wealth inequality may be relevant to population health beyond income inequality, although mechanisms and causality require further study.

item.title: Mental Health Ghost Networks in Commercial Insurance Plans
item.summary: IMPORTANCE: Whether network directories in commercial insurance plans, which cover the majority of insured US residents, reliably connect patients to mental health care has only seen limited testing. OBJECTIVE: To assess network directory accuracy, appointment availability, wait times, and travel burden for mental health clinicians listed in commercial insurance online plan directories. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: A cross-sectional study with a secret shopper design of 5822 calls to psychiatrists and psychologists listed in the online network directories of the largest commercial carrier in 5 diverse states (Delaware, Montana, New Jersey, Rhode Island, and Virginia), conducted between October 2025 and March 2026. Callers contacted the geographically closest listed clinician on behalf of a simulated patient assigned a standard preferred provider organization plan and a nonemergency mental health condition. Calls in which the caller could not obtain a definitive outcome were classified as nonevaluable. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Appointment availability with the listed clinician and with alternate clinicians, network directory inaccuracy by error type (contact information, specialty, network status), capacity limitations, wait time to appointment, and travel time to appointment. Reported percentages and means are adjusted (predicted) values with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 5822 calls, 3570 (61.3%) were nonevaluable, most commonly because callers reached only an answering machine or automated system. Among the 2252 evaluable calls, 23.6% (95% CI, 21.9%-25.4%) resulted in a scheduled appointment with the listed clinician, increasing to 32.1% (95% CI, 30.2%-34.1%) when alternate clinicians were included. Network directory inaccuracies affected 55.6% (95% CI, 53.6%-57.7%) of evaluable calls, with contact information errors (31.0%; 95% CI, 29.1%-32.9%) and specialty errors (22.2%; 95% CI, 20.6%-23.9%) being most prevalent. Capacity limitations prevented scheduling in 21.6% (95% CI, 19.9%-23.3%) of evaluable calls. Mean wait time was 20.5 days (95% CI, 18.0-23.0 days), with longer waits for psychiatry than psychology (22.5 vs 17.3 days). Mean travel time was 17.1 minutes (95% CI, 14.6-19.6 minutes) overall but 41.8 minutes (95% CI, 27.5-56.0 minutes) in Montana and 30.8 minutes (95% CI, 19.8-41.7 minutes) for rural residents. Across all initial call attempts, only 12.4% resulted in an appointment. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, access barriers previously documented in public insurance programs extend to the privately insured population, undermining the assumption that commercial coverage automatically translates into meaningful access to mental health care.

item.title: Psychotherapy and Antidepressant Use After the US Preventive Services Task Force-Recommended Depression Screening
item.summary: IMPORTANCE: Fewer than one-third of adults with depression receive any treatment for depression. It is important to evaluate the association between the 2016 US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommendation and depression treatment nationally. OBJECTIVE: To examine changes in the likelihood of psychotherapy and antidepressant use after the USPSTF-recommended routine adult depression screening. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This policy evaluation used a single-group, interrupted time series design with logistic regression. Medical Expenditure Panel Survey Household Component data from 2008 to 2023 were analyzed from November 3, 2025, to March 31, 2026. The sample included adults aged 18 years and older. EXPOSURE: 2016 USPSTF grade B recommendation for routine adult depression screening. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Likelihood of psychotherapy or antidepressant use immediately (level change) and over time (post-USPSTF slope change [trend]) using an interrupted time series design and logistic regression models. RESULTS: The analysis included 372 962 adults. Using the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey person-level survey weights, this corresponded to a nationally representative sample of 244 316 623 adults (median age, 47 years; IQR, 32-61 years; 51.6% female). The recommendation was associated with a significant level increase (odds ratio [OR], 1.18; 95% CI, 1.02-1.37) and post-USPSTF trend (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.04-1.11) increase in the likelihood of psychotherapy only, level (OR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.82-0.94) and post-USPSTF trend (OR, 0.98; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99) decreases in the likelihood of antidepressants only, and no significant changes in combined treatment among adults overall. By psychological distress level, it was associated with a significant level increase in the likelihood of psychotherapy only (OR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.10-2.41) and post-USPSTF trend decrease in the likelihood of antidepressants only (OR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.98) among adults reporting serious distress, significant level (OR, 1.38; 95% CI, 1.15-1.66) and post-USPSTF trend (OR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.01-1.10) increases in the probability of psychotherapy only, and level (OR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.81-0.96) and post-USPTF trend (OR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.98) decreases in the likelihood of antidepressants only among adults reporting mild or moderate distress, and no significant changes among adults reporting no distress. There was a significant level decrease (OR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.70-0.89) in the probability of seeing a prescriber for psychotherapy after the recommendation. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This study found that the USPSTF recommendation for routine adult depression screening was associated with increased likelihood of psychotherapy and decreased likelihood of antidepressant use among adults reporting some level of psychological distress. Findings suggest no association with unnecessary treatment among adults with low levels of distress.

item.title: Investing in pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response
item.summary: If resources for public health and decision makers are limited, what are the highest-priority investments they can make? Drawing on the Disease Control Priorities report on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response, in this Viewpoint we summarise our reflections and recommendations for the next decade in public health and focus on the highest return actions for pandemic preparedness, prevention, and response that countries can take to protect themselves and others. We identified 85 feasible national-level and local-level actions, categorising 40 of them as high-priority investments. At regional and global levels, we identified and recommend 33 high-priority actions. These investments could have pay-offs substantially exceeding their cost. Ensuring adequate funding will require countries to contribute according to their fiscal capacity, with some countries requiring external support. Importantly, financing response to an outbreak should be timely and therefore prearranged.

item.title: Are there grounds for optimism for the future of global health?
item.summary: In the past decade, the field of global health has faced severe challenges and intense scrutiny concerning its legitimacy and effectiveness. A longer-term perspective-200 years rather than 10-offers grounds for guarded optimism about the future of global health. A review of the history of international health reveals that although the self-interested agendas of industrialised states have been the dominant driving forces in the field, these pursuits have been tempered by the gradual cross-national diffusion of cosmopolitan norms and initiatives concerning the right to health for all and government responsibility to improve population health. The grounds for hope are not that progress is inevitable. Rather, universalist commitments might have become sufficiently widespread and institutionalised to withstand periods of political backlash without reversing long-term expansion. The key to sustaining progress will be that actors who are committed to these norms persist in defending them.

item.title: Reimagining the aspirations of public health for the coming decade
item.summary: The past 10 years have challenged and reshaped public health in ways that were difficult to imagine more than a decade ago. This situation calls on public health to think clearly about where the field is headed and to anticipate where the field needs to be so as to emerge stronger from the moment. Five trends will be shaping health in the coming decades: population ageing, urbanisation, climate change, changing relationships with institutions, and the emergence of transformative technology. These trends are driving-and coinciding with-shifting disease burden, including the rise of non-communicable diseases, the growing importance of neurological diseases and brain disorders, the continued and more unpredictable effects of infectious diseases, widening health gaps, and increasing demands on health systems. These challenges present clear opportunities and should focus public health on five key aspirations moving forward: creating longer, healthier lives through a reckoning with the conditions for healthy ageing, grappling with new-and primarily commercial-determinants of health, efforts to build better health systems, the embrace of new technologies, and a reimagination of how the field thinks, talks, acts, and communicates its work.

item.title: Addressing health equity and its major challenges
item.summary: Three major challenges confront public health: inequality, the climate crisis, and political instability. Four domains of recommendations, formulated to respond to the inequality-pandemic cycle, form the basis of what is needed to improve health and health equity. First, address the gross inequalities in the global, and national, economic architecture. Second, take action on the social determinants of health-the eight Marmot Principles provide an evidence-based guide to action. Third, ensure an equitable distribution of health-enhancing technology. Finally, enable community development. Marmot Places, which have been developed in England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland, are a way to combine domains two and four: taking action on social determinants of health at the local level. However, national action is required too, particularly on unfair economic arrangements.

item.title: Closing the implementation gap: prioritised, proactive, and accountable primary health care for the next decade
item.summary: Most preventable deaths in low-income and middle-income countries occur not because effective interventions are unknown or unaffordable but because health systems fail to deliver these interventions reliably. Primary health care is essential for public health: prevention, early detection, and treatment can reach entire populations. Nearly 50 years after the Alma-Ata Declaration, few primary health-care systems effectively prevent, detect, and treat the leading killers. Two forces make now the moment to act: the abrupt 2025 decrease in development assistance and new technologies that might improve the ability to deliver and measure care at low cost. To close this implementation gap, primary health care should be prioritised, proactive, and accountable. Prioritised primary health care within a commitment to universal primary health care should fund the highest-impact actions first with transparent, nationally owned selection, and with core essential medicines free at the point of dispensing. Proactive primary health care should reach, track, and support patients before and between visits. Accountable primary health care should judge success by health outcomes with financing aligned with population health goals. Preventable deaths should be reviewed without blame as never-events feeding into improved prioritisation. Delivering these actions requires a skilled and supported workforce, a reliable supply of medicines and diagnostics, sustained financing, community trust, and data that can drive action. Decide first which outcomes matter most, identify the actions that produce them, strengthen the system those actions require, and judge investment by health gained.

item.title: The epistemic crisis as the defining challenge of public health: knowledge, power, and the politics of truth
item.summary: Public health has always been a science in the service of politics-a discipline that translates evidence into collective action and knowledge into policy. But something qualitatively different is now under way. The next decade will not merely test the capacity of public health to respond to new threats, it will test the epistemic foundations on which the entire enterprise rests. The crisis we face is not primarily a crisis of evidence-there is more health research than ever-but of the authority of knowledge: who produces it, whose counts, and whether shared facts can still ground collective responses.

item.title: People at the centre
item.summary: Since the 2024 US presidential election disruption of many US institutions, numerous leadership shifts and budget reallocations and reductions, along with legislative and policy changes, have shaken public health global financial architecture, damaging institutional global and domestic roles. Crucially, this fraught time also offers an opportunity to renavigate the positioning of the field of public health and the directions taken more than a century ago. In the 19th century the biomedical model became dominant and public health greatly reduced its focus on adverse living conditions-the previous strategy that underpinned many foundational advances as progressive elements of the sanitary movement allied with social movements to achieve better living conditions. Years later, this positioning left public health largely silent on growing corporate influence, privatisation, and inequality in income and wealth. The enduring US racial hierarchy also adds to the long odds of placing people at the centre-the overarching goal of improving people's health.

item.title: Outcomes of Mindful Mood Balance for Moms, online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy for perinatal depressive relapse prevention in the USA: a two-arm, single-blind, pragmatic randomised clinical trial
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Effective and accessible approaches to prevent depressive relapse and reduce symptoms are crucial for addressing the major public health problem of depression among perinatal women. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of Mindful Mood Balance (MMB) for Moms plus usual care (hereafter MMB for Moms)-a web-based mindfulness-based cognitive therapy programme customised for perinatal women-compared with usual care only, in reducing depressive relapse and symptoms. METHODS: This single-blind, randomised clinical trial was done across the USA, in euthymic pregnant women with recurrent depression who were on recent or current antidepressant medication. Recruitment occurred from March 7, 2019, to July 8, 2020 (data collection was completed Sept 12, 2021). Participants were randomly assigned to MMB for Moms, or usual care. Primary outcomes were reduction in depressive relapse risk and symptom burden, assessed using the Mini International Neuropsychiatric Interview and Patient Health Questionaire-9, respectively, across the study period. Outcomes were assessed from baseline until 6-months postpartum in three phases (intervention, end of intervention to delivery, and postpartum). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03623620, and is complete. FINDINGS: Participants were recruited between March 7, 2019, and July 8, 2020. Data from 500 randomly assigned participants (mean age 32 years [SD 4·5] and mean 11·5 [2·8] weeks gestation), were analysed as the intention-to-treat sample. Of the 500 participants (249 assigned to MMB for Moms and 251 assigned to usual care), 383 [77%] provided assessment data at 3 months and 389 [78%] at 6 months postpartum. MMB for Moms had significantly lower risk of depressive relapse compared with usual care during the full trial period (up to 6 months postpartum): 81 (33%) of 249 participants assigned to MMB for Moms and 111 (44%) of 251 participants in usual care had depressive relapse (hazard ratio 0·74 [95% CI 0·56-0·99]; p=0·045; adjusted false discovery rate p=0·045). MMB for Moms was also associated with a significant reduction in depression symptom burden during the 12 week intervention phase (average decrease of 0·75 [SE 0·13] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·31 [0·13] in the usual care group) but not during the full trial period (average decrease of 0·61 [SE 0·18] in the MMB for Moms group and 0·54 [0·17] in the usual care group). INTERPRETATION: MMB for Moms resulted in lower risk of relapse compared with usual care, and lower depression symptom burden during the intervention phase, potentially offering an effective non-pharmacological support option for depression relapse prevention during the perinatal period with positive implications for public health practice. FUNDING: US National Institutes of Health and US National Institute of Mental Health.

item.title: A multifaceted intervention to increase bystander CPR rates after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in France: a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised, controlled trial
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) is a key determinant of survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but rates remain suboptimal worldwide. We evaluated whether a multifaceted intervention targeting emergency dispatch systems and community response could increase bystander-initiated CPR before emergency medical service (EMS) arrival. METHODS: We conducted a stepped-wedge, cluster-randomised trial in 15 French EMS agencies. The intervention combined dispatcher training for early recognition of cardiac arrest and telephone-assisted CPR, activation of trained volunteers through a geolocation smartphone application, and structured audit and feedback provided to EMS agencies. Consecutive adults (≥18 years) with non-traumatic OHCA were included. Randomisation was stratified by tercile of OHCA volume managed by each EMS in 2015. The intervention was implemented during a 1-month transition period before the intervention period at each EMS centre. A dedicated protocol guided dispatchers to identify cardiac arrest from unresponsiveness and abnormal breathing, then gave scripted compression-only instructions and activated volunteers, targeting recognition within 60 s of call pick-up and first compression within a further 60 s. The primary outcome was bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival. The trial was prospectively registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03633370) and is completed. FINDINGS: Of the 15 EMS agencies initially randomised, two withdrew before recruitment began and were replaced, and one enrolled no patients. Therefore, between Aug 27, 2018, and Feb 20, 2022, 14 EMS agencies recruited a total of 2160 patients. The intention-to-treat analysis included 1684 patients (686 control, 998 intervention) enrolled across the 12 originally randomised EMS agencies. The mean age for all patients included in the intention-to-treat analysis was 67 years (SD 15), and 1205 (71·6%) were male. Bystander-initiated CPR before EMS arrival occurred in 421 (61·4%) patients in the control group and 708 (70·9%) patients in the intervention group (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1·54 [95% CI 1·09-2·19]; p=0·017). Estimates were consistent across six prespecified sensitivity analyses (OR range, 1·38-1·55), remaining significant in four, but not after adjustment for cluster-specific secular trends (1·38 [0·98-1·94]) or baseline characteristics (1·39 [0·97-1·98]). No intervention-related adverse events were reported. INTERPRETATION: A multifaceted intervention was associated with increased bystander-initiated CPR after OHCA, although the estimate was sensitive to the modelling of secular trends, and it did not translate into improved clinical outcomes. These findings support further investigation of coordinated community-based strategies to strengthen the early links in the chain of survival at a population level. FUNDING: Direction Générale de l'Offre de Soins.

item.title: The effect of food taxes in the UK on health and economic outcomes, and equity: a modelling study
item.summary: BACKGROUND: WHO recommends using fiscal policies (such as taxes on unhealthy foods) that discourage consuming foods that contribute to unhealthy diets. Food tax evaluations require consideration for sociodemographic differences, consumer and industry behaviour, reformulation, and long-term health-related outcomes and health inequalities. We aimed to model the potential benefits and harms of three food tax policy designs, to health, costs, and inequalities, in the UK. METHODS: Using a microsimulation model, we performed an economic evaluation of three UK food tax policy designs: (1) a Sugar Snacks tax targeting snacks, cakes, and milk drinks; (2) an Unhealthy Food tax high in fat, sugar, or salt; and (3) a Sugar and Salt tax. Consumption and nutritional changes for a UK representative synthetic population (aged ≥5 years) were estimated by applying a hierarchical Almost Ideal Demand System, accommodating key socio-demographic differences. Our primary analysis simulated outcomes for consumer response only. Secondary analyses incorporated industry responses in the model. The microsimulation estimated changes to weight, cardiometabolic risk factors, lifetime health, discounted National Health Service (NHS) costs, social care costs, unemployment or inactivity, and social benefit receipts. FINDINGS: The estimated average reduction in daily calorie intake was -25 kcal (95% credible interval [95% CrI]; -31 to -19), -42 kcal (-51 to -33), and -58 kcal (-66 to -50) for the Sugar Snacks, Unhealthy Food, and Sugar and Salt taxes respectively, with reductions in sugar, salt, and saturated fat. Long-term modelling showed improved health, including reduced cardiovascular disease, and type 2 diabetes for all three tax policies. The taxes reduced NHS costs (Sugar Snacks -£168 [95% CrI -461 to -73], Unhealthy Food -£268 [-722 to -105], and Sugar and Salt -£374 [-1033 to -159]) and social care costs. The impact on health inequalities varied by policy design. Only the Sugar and Salt tax had a positive impact on health inequalities. INTERPRETATION: The overall health impact of each of the three tax policy designs modelled was positive, but it can be associated with important nutritional trade-off-cross-price elasticities led to a reduction in fibre intake. Of the three policies modelled, the Sugar and Salt tax generated the greatest gains and reduced health inequalities. Policy design should consider potential impacts on health inequalities and should be part of a multi-component strategy. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research.

item.title: Association between parental death during childhood and health and wellbeing in adulthood in 22 countries and regions: a retrospective, outcome-wide analysis
item.summary: BACKGROUND: Clinical and epidemiological evidence suggests that adults who have experienced the death of a parent or caregiver in childhood are at elevated risk for adverse health outcomes. The aim of this study was to examine cross-national variation in indicators of health and wellbeing among adults who experienced the death of a parent by age 12 years. METHODS: In this retrospective, outcome-wide analysis, we analysed data from Wave 1 of the Global Flourishing Study, a 5-year pre-registered longitudinal panel study (2024-28) of nationally representative adult participants (N=202 898) aged 18 years and older using probability-sampling across 22 geographically and culturally diverse countries and regions (ie, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Egypt, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kenya, Mexico, Nigeria, the Philippines, Poland, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Tanzania, Türkiye, the UK, and the USA) to examine associations between retrospectively recalled parental death during childhood (yes or no) and current health and wellbeing. We conducted a series of country and region-specific weighted multivariable regression using an outcome-wide design. Random effects meta-analyses were used to pool country and region-specific effect estimates for 69 wellbeing outcomes. FINDINGS: Meta-analysed associations across 22 countries and regions suggested that participants who experienced the death of a parent by age 12 years, relative to those who did not, reported more age-normalised health impairments (risk ratio [RR] 1·14 [95% CI 1·04 to 1·25]), more anxiety and depression symptoms (RR 1·09 [1·01 to 1·17] and RR 1·08 [1·01 to 1·15], respectively), more loneliness (standardised effect estimate [B] 0·06 [95% CI 0·01 to 0·10]), reduced sense of meaning (B -0·05 [-0·08 to -0·01], and reduced wellbeing (for example a lower sense of being at peace [RR 0·96 (95% CI 0·92 to 0·99)]). Country-specific effect estimates varied in magnitude. INTERPRETATION: Parental bereavement in childhood can affect health and wellbeing in adulthood, with some cross-national variation in the magnitude of adverse effects. Parental death during childhood is an important determinant of health across the lifespan and as such public health policies are needed to support a population-wide approach to bereavement care that spans health, social, and economic domains. FUNDING: John Templeton Foundation, Templeton Religion Trust, Templeton World Charity Foundation, Fetzer Institute, Paul Foster Family Foundation, Wellbeing for Planet Earth Foundation, Well Being Trust, and the David and Carol Myers Foundation.

item.title: The north-south divide in English mortality, 1981-2024: a longitudinal population study
item.summary: BACKGROUND: The north-south mortality divide in England, UK, has persisted for several decades. Previous longitudinal analyses up to 2016 have highlighted a widening mortality gap among those aged 25-44 years since the mid-1990s. We aimed to update mortality trends in England and evaluate how trends differed by age and sex up to 2024. METHODS: We did a segmented longitudinal population study of the north-south mortality divide in England (1981-2024). Using registered deaths and mid-year population estimates by 5-year age group and sex, we calculated standardised mortality rates and estimated adjusted north-south rate ratios using within-year Poisson models. We used segmented Poisson regression to compare mortality trends between 2010-19 and 2020-24. FINDINGS: Despite overall declines in mortality, interrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, the north-south mortality divide persisted during 1981-2024, widening among both female and male individuals aged 25-49 years. During 2010-19, northern excess mortality among those aged 25-49 years increased per year for female individuals (incidence rate ratio 1·018 [95% CI 1·013-1·022]) and male individuals (1·012 [1·009-1·016]). During 2020-24, these trends continued: Poisson models suggested a slowing among female individuals aged 25-49 years (0·987 [0·975-0·999]) and further widening among male individuals younger than 75 years (1·004 [1·000-1·007]), but neither change was robust to allowance for overdispersion, and the gap did not narrow in any age or sex group. By 2024, northern excess mortality reached 25·9% (95% CI 24·7-27·1) for those younger than 75 years, and 42·4% (38·5-46·3) for those aged 25-49 years. INTERPRETATION: Over the past four decades, England's regional mortality inequalities have widened among working‑age adults, with more rapid increases among female individuals than male individuals up to 2020 (before the COVID-19 pandemic). Pre-pandemic trends continued through 2020-24, with no narrowing of the north-south gap in any age or sex group by 2024. Reducing the north-south health divide will require sustained large-scale action across central government and regional authorities. FUNDING: National Institute for Health and Care Research, British Heart Foundation, and The Pandemic Institute.

item.title: Aging Out of Coverage: Lessons From the West Virginia $1,000 Adult Dental Benefit
item.summary: This paper studies the utilization of dental services during the recent implementation of an adult (age 21 and over) Medicaid dental benefit in West Virginia. We analyze claims data and find: (1) before implementation, quarterly utilization of preventative and restorative services falls from 8% at age 20 to virtually 0% at age 21; (2) post-implementation, utilization falls from 8% at age 20 to 5% at age 21, implying a net increase of 50% of baseline utilization; (3) the net effect of the dental benefit is significantly larger in counties with a larger number of oral health care provider practices. Our results provide evidence that public health insurance expansions are dampened in markets with a limited supply of provider practices.

item.title: Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity: The Role of Maternal Comorbidities
item.summary: The U.S. maternal health crisis disproportionately affects Black women, who face nearly twice the risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) compared with White women. Using 2016-2022 Texas hospital discharge data and a validated obstetric comorbidity score, the analysis first documents that the prevalence of SMM increased by 18% between 2016 and 2022, whereas maternal comorbidity burden increased by 42% over the same period. To better assess the role of comorbidities, the comorbidity score is disaggregated into underlying health and pregnancy-specific conditions. Oaxaca-Blinder decompositions indicate that the former accounts for the largest share-49 to 53%-of the Black-White SMM gap, while the latter accounts for an additional third of the disparity. After accounting for these factors, a residual Black-White SMM gap of 17%-20% persists across and within hospitals, including among women treated by the same physician. Overall, the findings underscore the critical need to improve women's health well before childbirth hospitalization and throughout the reproductive life course, while also strengthening prenatal care to prevent and effectively manage conditions that arise during pregnancy.

item.title: The Impact of Repealing Certificate-of-Need Laws on Healthcare Spending: A Causal Analysis
item.summary: Certificate-of-Need laws in 35 US states require healthcare providers to obtain government approval before building new facilities or expanding services. Their stated goal is to ensure a genuine community need and avoid redundant services, with the aim of controlling healthcare costs and distributing resources fairly, although their effectiveness is debated. Our study differs from previous literature as we present the causal effects of repealing Certificate-of-Need laws on various healthcare expenses using modern difference-in-differences techniques and event studies. Our findings suggest that repealing Certificate-of-Need laws can reduce the burden of healthcare spending.

item.title: Multiple paths to privatisation in healthcare? Comparing England and Italy beyond the public-private divide
item.summary: English and Italian national health systems are predominantly funded by general taxation and treat patients primarily free at the point of delivery. Both healthcare systems are facing increasing financial pressures given population ageing, the rise in chronic and non-communicable diseases, and fiscal restraint. In recent years, pressures on public healthcare have revived debate around the role of the private sector, but discussion is mired in a lack of conceptual clarity. We seek to bring greater analytical order by distinguishing seven distinct 'trajectories of privatisation', each reflecting different modes and logics of interaction between public and private actors. We examine two similar health systems - England and Italy - highlight their similarities and differences regarding emerging and established trajectories. There is less evidence of 'hard privatisation', seen as the private share of overall spending; however, both countries are experiencing greater use of on-demand staff and financialisation. In both systems subtler privatisation dynamics (public-private partnerships, managerialism, and entrepreneurialism) are redefining and blurring the boundaries between public and private provision. Public perceptions of perceived privatisation are shaped by direct, tangible experiences of care and out-of-pocket spending. Some privatisation dynamics are mainly driven by behaviour of patients, professionals, and investors rather than by policies.

item.title: The role of program and policy level interventions in addressing intention to leave and turnover among health workers in Ethiopia - a repeated cross-sectional study
item.summary: BACKGROUND: High levels of health workers' intention to leave and turnover continue to undermine health workforce availability and health system performance, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Ethiopia has implemented a series of national Human Resources for Health (HRH) policy and programmatic interventions aimed at improving health worker motivation, retention and working conditions. This study compared intention to leave and turnover among selected health professionals between 2014 and 2022 and explored changes observed during the implementation period of these interventions. METHODS: A repeated cross-sectional mixed-methods study was conducted using nationally representative surveys in 2014 and 2022. Both surveys employed the same structured questionnaire and a two-stage cluster sampling design, with sample sizes calculated assuming a 95% confidence level, 5% margin of error and 10% non-response rate. The 2014 survey included 1,356 health workers from 224 health facilities, while the 2022 survey included 1,754 health workers from 176 facilities. In addition, qualitative key informant interviews were conducted in 2022 with health sector leaders, managers and health workers involved in implementing HRH motivation and retention interventions to provide contextual insights into the quantitative findings. Quantitative data were analysed using SPSS, while qualitative data were analysed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: Between 2014 and 2022, intention to leave declined from 49.0% to 17.5% (absolute reduction: 31.5% points; p < 0.001), while the annual turnover rate decreased from 4.5% to 3.5% (absolute reduction: 1.0% point; p < 0.001) among medical doctors, health officers, nurses, midwives and anaesthetists. Similar reductions were observed in both hospitals (47.3% to 17.9%) and health centres (51.4% to 16.1%). Annual turnover also declined among medical doctors, nurses and anaesthetists. Key informants perceived improvements in selected financial and non-financial incentive packages, training opportunities, supportive supervision and workplace allowances. However, inadequate housing, unfair supervisory practices, low salaries, increasing costs of living and workplace safety concerns remained important challenges affecting workforce retention. CONCLUSIONS: Substantial reductions in health workers' intention to leave and turnover were observed during the implementation period of Ethiopia's national HRH policy and programmatic interventions. Although qualitative findings suggest perceived improvements in several workforce retention strategies, the repeated cross-sectional design does not permit causal attribution of the observed changes to the interventions. Persistent concerns regarding remuneration, housing, supervision and rising living costs indicate that continued investment in both financial and non-financial retention strategies remains essential for strengthening Ethiopia's health workforce.

item.title: Regional Disparities in the Efficiency of Guangdong's health service system: A Three-Stage DEA Evaluation Based on Data from 2015 to 2024
item.summary: BACKGROUND: China's healthcare reform has shifted its focus toward enhancing quality and systemic efficiency, yet significant regional disparities persist. Guangdong Province offers a critical case for examining health service efficiency inequalities due to its pronounced internal development gap between the Pearl River Delta (PRD) and the Eastern, Western, and Northern regions. OBJECTIVE: The objective of this study is to systematically evaluate the efficiency of the health service system in Guangdong Province from 2015 to 2024. The study will identify regional disparities and isolate the impact of external environmental factors in order to reveal performance after adjusting for observed environmental factors and statistical noise. METHODS: A three-stage Data Envelopment Analysis (DEA) model was employed to assess the efficiency of 21 prefecture-level cities in Guangdong. The input-oriented BCC model was utilized in the initial stage to obtain preliminary efficiency scores. In the second stage, Stochastic Frontier Analysis (SFA) was employed to adjust input slacks for environmental variables (GDP per capita and population density). The third stage of the process involved a re-evaluation of efficiency, with the inputs being adjusted accordingly. The input variables encompassed medical technical personnel, hospital beds, and medical institutions; the output variables comprised outpatient visits, inpatient cases, average length of stay, and bed utilization rate. A Malmquist Productivity Index analysis was also conducted to capture dynamic productivity changes over the study period. RESULTS: The initial DEA revealed an average technical efficiency (TE) of 0.929. Following adjustment, the mean TE increased to 0.932, indicating a slight underestimation due to unfavorable environmental factors. Scale efficiency (SE, mean = 0.986) was consistently higher than pure technical efficiency (PTE, mean = 0.946). After adjusting for observed environmental factors, the PTE estimates, which served as composite indicators of operational performance, suggested that dimensions related to management and technology represented the primary bottleneck. Significant regional disparities were confirmed, with the PRD region demonstrating superior and more resilient efficiency (adjusted TE = 0.948) compared to Eastern (0.902), Western (0.924), and Northern (0.933) Guangdong. And the period following the onset of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic coincided with a notable decline in PTE after 2019, highlighting systemic vulnerabilities. Malmquist analysis revealed that total factor productivity declined by 2.5% annually over the decade, associated primarily with technological regression (TC = 0.972) rather than efficiency losses. Productivity dropped by17.7% in 2019-2020, temporally aligned with the pandemic's onset, though sustained recovery occurred after 2022 with TFP reaching 1.047 in 2022-2023 and 1.042 in 2023-2024. Considerable heterogeneity existed across cities, with Dongguan achieving positive TFP growth (1.003) while most others experienced declines. CONCLUSION: The health service system of Guangdong has achieved a relatively balanced scale of resource allocation. However, it encounters challenges with regard to managerial and technical performance. It is recommended that policy interventions shift focus from quantitative expansion to the enhancement of intrinsic operational capabilities, particularly in Eastern, Western, and Northern Guangdong, while also prioritizing technological innovation to address the systemic technological regression identified in this study.
